<thought>Since the template searches for breaking the ester bond returned no results, I will look for a more general disconnection that breaks an ether (the O‑C bond linking the side‑chain to the cyclohexane). This type of transformation is common (e.g., a Williamson ether synthesis in the forward direction). By breaking the ether we obtain two fragments that are both simple, commercially available building blocks: a cyclohexanol derivative and a poly‑unsaturated carboxylic acid. I will search for templates that break an “ether oxygens” group and form an “aliphatic hydroxyl” and an “alkene” (the side‑chain).</thought>
